cases.title: Iliofemoral DVT and iliac vein compression
cases.stem: A 34-year-old woman has extensive acute left iliofemoral DVT with severe pain and swelling. She has a low bleeding risk.

questions.question: Which feature makes adjunctive endovascular thrombus removal reasonable to consider?
options: Extensive symptomatic iliofemoral DVT in a fit patient with low bleeding risk
questions.explanation: Selected patients with extensive symptomatic iliofemoral DVT may benefit from rapid thrombus removal.

questions.question: After thrombus removal, severe compression of the left common iliac vein is demonstrated. Which treatment may be appropriate?
options: Venous stenting of the obstructive lesion when anatomy and clinical context are suitable
Embolisation of the inferior vena cava
questions.explanation: Treating a significant iliac outflow obstruction can improve venous drainage and reduce recurrence.
questions.imageQuery: iliac vein compression venography stent May-Thurner

questions.question: What can intravascular ultrasound add in this setting?
options: Assessment of venous calibre, compression and stent landing zones
questions.explanation: IVUS can improve characterisation of venous obstruction and guide stent sizing/position.

questions.question: After successful intervention, anticoagulation:
options: Usually remains an important component of treatment unless contraindicated
questions.explanation: Endovascular therapy does not routinely remove the need for appropriate antithrombotic treatment.

questions.question: When placing an iliac venous stent, which technical principle is important for durable patency?
options: Secure adequate inflow and outflow and cover the obstructive lesion appropriately
Leave a severe untreated inflow lesion
Terminate the stent within the tightest stenosis
Avoid assessing the contralateral venous anatomy
questions.explanation: Durable venous reconstruction depends on treating the entire relevant obstruction while preserving adequate inflow and outflow.

cases.title: Dysfunctional haemodialysis fistula
cases.stem: A haemodialysis patient has falling access flows and elevated venous pressures. Ultrasound shows a significant outflow stenosis in an AV fistula.

questions.question: What is the role of fistulography?
options: Define stenoses and venous outflow anatomy
questions.explanation: Fistulography maps the access circuit and identifies lesions amenable to endovascular treatment.

questions.question: A focal significant stenosis is demonstrated. What is the usual first treatment?
questions.explanation: Balloon angioplasty is the principal treatment for many haemodialysis-access stenoses.

questions.question: When may a stent or stent-graft be considered?
options: Recoil, rupture or selected recurrent lesions depending on location
questions.explanation: Stent-grafts have specific indications, including selected recurrent stenoses and treatment of rupture.

questions.question: What should technical success include?
options: Improved angiographic and haemodynamic flow through the access
questions.explanation: The goal is restoration of useful access flow with correction of the culprit lesion.

questions.question: Why must the underlying stenosis be treated when declotting a thrombosed dialysis access?
options: Untreated outflow or anastomotic stenosis predisposes to early rethrombosis
Thrombectomy permanently cures every access lesion
The stenosis is unrelated to thrombosis
questions.explanation: Successful declotting requires treatment of the lesion responsible for stasis or access dysfunction.

questions.question: A major advantage of stenting in severe malignant superior vena cava syndrome is:
questions.explanation: Stenting can rapidly improve venous congestion and symptoms.

questions.question: A retrievable IVC filter should generally be:
options: Removed when the indication has resolved and retrieval is technically feasible
Used instead of anticoagulation in all DVT
questions.explanation: Retrieval when no longer required reduces long-term filter-related complications.

questions.question: The objective of recanalising a chronic venous occlusion is to:
options: Restore a continuous lumen with adequate inflow and outflow
Embolise all collaterals before crossing the lesion
questions.explanation: A durable venous reconstruction requires satisfactory inflow, conduit and outflow.

questions.question: Sclerotherapy is an appropriate percutaneous treatment for:
options: Every high-flow AVM without haemodynamic assessment
questions.explanation: Low-flow venous malformations may respond to image-guided sclerotherapy; flow characteristics must be established first.

questions.question: Before treating a high-flow arteriovenous malformation, which feature must be understood?
questions.explanation: The angioarchitecture and haemodynamics determine access, embolic strategy and risk.

questions.question: Real-time ultrasound guidance for vascular access allows the operator to:
options: Visualise the target vessel, needle and adjacent structures
Eliminate the need for sterile technique
questions.explanation: Direct visualisation improves procedural accuracy and reduces mechanical complications.

questions.question: When thrombectomy of a haemodialysis access is performed, what else is important?
options: Identify and treat the underlying causative stenosis
questions.explanation: Failure to correct the underlying lesion predisposes to early rethrombosis.

questions.question: Which angiographic sign suggests venous rupture during angioplasty?
questions.explanation: Extravasation indicates loss of vessel-wall integrity and may require balloon tamponade or stent-graft treatment.

questions.question: Which feature makes a venous intervention more likely to fail if left untreated?
options: Poor inflow or persistent outflow obstruction
questions.explanation: Venous reconstruction requires adequate inflow and outflow; residual obstructive disease compromises patency.

questions.question: Which lesion is a typical indication for image-guided musculoskeletal biopsy?
options: An indeterminate bone or soft-tissue mass where histology will influence management
A simple asymptomatic bone island with classic imaging
questions.explanation: Biopsy is indicated when tissue diagnosis will change management and a safe route is available.
